title: Karur Vysya Bank Ltd - 590003 - Transcript of Conference Call

summary.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
summary.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

financial_highlights.value: 0.43% annualised (INR94 crores NPA/standard/restructured + INR25 crores floating provision)

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ led by mortgages (+12% QoQ) and personal loans (+11% QoQ); retail jewel loans fell 1% to a total jewel book of INR32,153 crores (29% of advances), with LTV of 67% for agri gold and 59% for non-agri gold.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional
segments.commentary: Portfolio grew 12% QoQ (14% of advances), with average ticket size of INR42 crores; credit substitutes grew about INR500 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial business (SBG and BBG)
segments.commentary: Grew 8% QoQ, with disbursements up about 24% QoQ; tailor-made products (GST surrogate, open term loan) crossed INR450 crores outstanding.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits up 5% QoQ; CASA rose INR1,489 crores in Q2 (current accounts +INR592 crores, savings +INR897 crores); retail term deposits 73% of total deposits, growing 6% QoQ (+INR3,902 crores).

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri loans grew 4% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of the agri book.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 18-20% for FY27 (YTD 13%); management cautioned that YTD growth is not an indicator for full-year growth.
NIM for FY27 guided at 4% plus; management said it expects to cross 4% for the next 2 quarters but would not commit to 4.26% being retained.
ROA for FY27 guided at about 2%, with 2.1% reported for Q2.
GNPA guided below 1.5%, NNPA below 1%, slippages below 1%; cost-to-income expected below 45% over the next 2 quarters.
Branch expansion: 50 branches planned for FY27, with 26 to be opened by end-December 2026 and the balance by year-end.
Liquidity coverage ratio to be maintained in the 115-120% range versus 129% reported.
capex_capacity: 20 branches opened in H1 FY27 (including 2 in Q1); 50 planned for FY27.
Branch expansion focus: South India first, then Maharashtra and Gujarat, then Central and North, and East last.
Working capital utilisation steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years; US-export textile borrowers at about 55-56% utilisation.
Management sees little customer capex or textile modernisation demand currently.
demand_pricing: Credit demand in corporate and institutional segment came from EPC, infrastructure, commercial real estate, capital market participants and selective textile and NBFC capex.
Textile portfolio is about 5% of advances; split is 40% upstream (spinning/ginning), 22% midstream, 38% downstream (finished goods and apparel), with downstream most exposed to US tariffs.
Bank is seeing poaching in mortgages from banks offering lower rates; management chose not to match and accepted some account losses, while housing loans were also de-emphasised.
Vehicle loans trending down as a tactical choice: higher delinquency, 150% risk weight, and funding tightness; funds redirected to gold and mortgages.

Management expects pricing competition from banks flush with FCNR-driven liquidity, which may bring down yields; EBLR book rose to 57% of advances from 55%, fixed-rate book 34%, MCLR book fell to 7% from 9%.
Yield on investments fell 4 bps to 6.79%.
